evidence: Source review only; no full configured judge run is claimed. tests/test.sh:203-227 runs the gates suite before the scored suite on the same app, with max-concurrent-agent 1. Render's criterion at gates/render/judge.toml:23 uses a new draft and says not to save. Constraints' criterion at gates/constraints/judge.toml:32 creates and leaves one saved gate record. The shared app_context.md:3-7 explicitly says titles identify server records, later criteria retain independent credit, and judges must not assume an empty library or delete a gate record. All dimension prompts direct fresh scratch drafts and avoiding unrelated saved records; functional/prompt.md additionally says the gate already established a clean-context Save and to avoid repeating its fixture. Functional/judge.toml:203 creates a new identity for its restart/readback check, and :212-221 use valid revision histories rather than assuming the first library item is pristine. Polish criteria at polish/judge.toml:23-32 can operate on current controls and a new unsaved draft; visual criteria at visual/judge.toml:24-43 judge current rendered appearance and explicitly disregard arbitrary authored preview content. I challenged the sequence with a single-record app: it could satisfy the gate's first save but would fail the functional new-record save, so earlier mutation does not give it false credit. A conforming app with the gate record plus a later saved record remains gradable by the new record's identity; the phrase 'one record' in functional/judge.toml:203 is read as one matching identity under app_context.md:3-5, not a demand that the whole library contain only one. No pristine-seed dependency was found. The raw-evidence index was absent at review time, so cross-dimension execution remains unmeasured outside this source-wording verdict.
